name: Melodic death metal: brighter, more presence

provenance.rationale: More presence and articulation, less aggressive fizz suppression, scooped-to-flat mids allowed.

status: PRIOR / UNCALIBRATED hypothesis (not measured on a reference); numbers need lead approval, then calibration with the user's references

analysis.spectrum: LTAS, 1/3-octave (IEC nominal centres), Welch, Hann, 8192-pt at 48 kHz, 50% overlap
analysis.activityGate: frames whose short-term RMS (50 ms) is within 30 dB of the 95th-percentile frame
analysis.normalization: levels in dB relative to the 1 kHz band
analysis.groupLevel: power mean of the bands in the group, in dB

rules.why: avoid flub; leave room for bass
HM-2 character is a broad mid push (500 Hz–2 kHz plateau), not a scoop
mids not honky relative to the saw band

buzz.def: spectral flatness (geometric/arithmetic mean of power) over 1–3 kHz on active frames

lowTightnessMs.def: median time for 80–160 Hz band energy to fall 20 dB after detected onsets

loudnessRangeLU.def: EBU R128 LRA-style short-term loudness range

gapNoiseDb.def: RMS in gate-closed gaps (bottom 5% frames) relative to active RMS

notes: Rules are evaluated on the post-cab output. The bus/master chain of a full mix is not modelled; when comparing to a reference recording, use the per-band LTAS difference (A-weighted 80 Hz–8 kHz) rather than these absolute rules.
Tolerance means a rule passes if violated by at most toleranceDb (reported as 'marginal').
Hypothesis: brighter than swedish_death_hm2; presence near the saw band, fizz less suppressed.
